method: Source and specification review only. No tests, builds, network writes, tracked edits, or commits were performed.

findings.title: Existing hook symlink target can change without changing the Git internals digest
findings.rationale: entryDigest returns only link:<readlink> for symlinks. An existing .git/hooks/pre-commit symlink to ../../scripts/hook.sh has the same digest after the engine edits scripts/hook.sh. The target is a normal tracked source file, so findViolations does not reject the edit. callEngine accepts the unchanged internals digest and runEngineTasks subsequently invokes git commit, which executes the modified target.
reproduction: Create a trusted clean repository with executable scripts/hook.sh and .git/hooks/pre-commit symlinked to ../../scripts/hook.sh.
Simulate an engine edit of scripts/hook.sh that writes a harmless temporary marker when executed, without modifying the symlink or Git configuration.
Take gitInternals again and verify equal digest; verify findInternalsChange returns undefined and findViolations has no findings.
Run a temporary-repository commit and observe marker creation.
findings.limitation: No runtime reproduction was executed. Precondition is a pre-existing executable linked hook. This is a gap in protection against changed hook code, not evidence of an attack against the current repository. The implementation follows explicit REQ-204 policy; this finding concerns the protection claim and policy scope, not a demonstrated implementation violation.
findings.recommendation: Treat the effective linked-hook target as a documented trust boundary or propose a specification change to protect effective executable hook targets. Do not change the implementation contrary to REQ-204.
findings.specification: openspec/changes/fix-guard-review-findings/specs/run-guards/spec.md REQ-204 explicitly requires symlinks in the hooks directory be compared by link text without following them, including dangling links and links to directories. The wording covers file symlinks as well; it does not restrict the rule to directory-valued symlinks.

findings.title: Git hook snapshot can block on a FIFO outside the external-operation supervisor
findings.rationale: filesUnder returns any non-directory entry. entryDigest performs readFileSync for all non-symlinks without requiring a regular file or using O_NONBLOCK. A FIFO added under .git/hooks causes the post-engine snapshot to block opening/reading it. The run deadline is applied to external processes, not this synchronous filesystem read, so it cannot terminate the wait.
reproduction: Use a disposable Linux repository and create a named pipe at .git/hooks/review-pipe with no writer.
Call gitInternals in a separately supervised child process.
Observe that the child does not return within a short harness deadline and terminate the child externally.
findings.limitation: Static control-flow finding; no FIFO was created and no blocking experiment was run. Requires POSIX special-file creation permission. Windows behavior was not evaluated.
findings.recommendation: Require regular files for hook content reads, reject special entries before opening, and use bounded/no-follow/nonblocking reader semantics. Also bound hook entry count and bytes if snapshot resource guarantees are intended.

findings.title: Normally exiting engine can leave background descendants alive after guards and run completion
findings.rationale: runClaude creates a POSIX process group, but invokes stop only on timeout, interruption, or output overflow. Its close handler clears the deadline and resolves without terminating the group. A same-group descendant using ignored/closed stdout and stderr does not hold the engine pipes open, so engine close can occur while that descendant remains active. The external-operation supervisor already kills its group on normal direct-child exit, whereas the engine implementation does not. Delayed descendant writes can occur after the post-engine snapshot and mutation guard.
reproduction: Use a fake engine that spawns a non-detached child with stdio:'ignore', records the child PID, and exits 0.
Have the child wait and then write a harmless marker.
Call runClaude with a deadline longer than the fake engine startup and await its successful result.
Check child PID liveness and delayed marker creation after return, then clean up the group from the harness.
findings.limitation: Missing cleanup is confirmed by source review; PID survival and timed guard bypass were not executed. Process-group escape is a separately documented environmental limitation and is not needed for this scenario.
findings.recommendation: Clean up the engine process group on every direct-child exit, including success, and wait for cleanup before returning. Test that a same-group descendant with independent stdio cannot remain alive after a successful engine call.

findings.title: Documented container prerequisite for --skip-permissions is stronger than implementation
findings.rationale: The document says both detected container and LOOMAKE_SANDBOX=1 are required. prepare.ts:47 checks only the environment variable for this option. The later outside-container flow permits interactive confirmation to continue. That behavior follows current REQ-121 and REQ-122, so changing the document to match is the direct correction; enforcing a new container prohibition would require a specification change.
reproduction: Read prepare.ts:47-51 and its later !inContainer interactive confirmation branch.
Compare openspec/specs/run/spec.md requirements sourced from REQ-121 and REQ-122 with docs/security.md:27.
findings.recommendation: Document the environment declaration gate and separate outside-container warning/confirmation behavior accurately.

already_protected.evidence: input.ts validates limits, rejects symlinks/special direct inputs, uses O_NOFOLLOW/O_NONBLOCK where available, checks file descriptor type, and enforces byte/entry/depth limits.
already_protected.scope_limit: Ancestor symlinks, complete filesystem isolation, and every input path are explicitly not claimed in docs/security.md.

already_protected.boundary: External command argument boundaries and control output
already_protected.evidence: runExternal passes argument arrays to a separate supervisor, separates target stdout/stderr from control fd3, bounds combined output, and applies operation/run deadlines.
already_protected.scope_limit: Configured quality commands intentionally execute trusted shell content.

already_protected.evidence: Lock creation uses wx and owner tokens, recovery checks host/PID; reuse validates single evidence-only parent commit, evidence schema/result/parent SHA/filename/document snapshots.
already_protected.scope_limit: These are integrity checks for trusted local state, not publisher signatures or protection from concurrent same-user adversaries.

already_protected.evidence: pr.ts rejects non-HTTPS, credentials, query/hash, whitespace, and invalid pull path shape; list results must be unique and match base/head and non-cross-repository metadata.
already_protected.scope_limit: Hostname is not pinned, consistent with potential enterprise GitHub use; no automatic navigation or execution of returned URLs was observed.

already_protected.evidence: mask.ts covers listed known token formats, JSON-decoded escaped strings, truncated JSON tails, streaming Bearer tokens and private keys. run.ts masks stdout/progress; logs.ts masks saved records.
already_protected.scope_limit: Arbitrary passwords, PII and actual deployed engine output were not audited; docs make the format-based limitation explicit.

already_protected.evidence: init.ts checks intended outputs including .gitignore for dangling links or project-external resolved ancestors before reading conflicting output content.
already_protected.scope_limit: Initial manifest reads and resource limits are documented as outside common-reader coverage; concurrent path replacement was not dynamically tested.

limits: This is an AI static review, not a human external security audit.
No finding has a dynamic reproduction result from this reviewer. Parent should reproduce in isolated fixtures before remediation acceptance.
The worktree had concurrent test-only edits by other agents. Findings reference product sources read during this review and should be checked against final source hashes.
No Windows/macOS execution, actual Claude Code session, actual GitHub authentication/publication, penetration test, or network behavior was performed.
No assertion that all possible vulnerabilities are absent is made, and no numeric security score is assigned.
reproduction_execution: Prepared only; not executed pending parent full-gate completion.

findings.policy: REQ-204 explicitly requires links inside the hook directory be compared by link text without following them.

parentRuntime.note: Parent independently inspected harness, added missing staging and regular-file FIFO control, then ran. All3 reproduced; temporary files removed and owned running PIDs killed. Linked hook is intentional policy gap, not current REQ204 violation.

userDecision: Approved recommended proposal: new specification for normal POSIX engine group cleanup and special hook file refusal; keep REQ204 link-text policy and document trust limits.
